title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm_rep_segalsemigroup}
The map $f\in{\mathcal{S}}\mapsto {\mathbf{T}}_f$ is differentiable with differential
\[D_{\rm v}{\mathbf{T}}_f = -{\mathbf{T}}_f\circ{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm w},\qquad {\rm w} = \tfrac{v(z)}{f'(z)}\,\partial_z,\]
where ${\rm v}=v(z)\partial_z$ is any holomorphic vector field on ${\mathbb{D}}$ with $v(0)=0$. More precisely, given a differentiable family $t\mapsto f_t\in{\mathcal{S}}$ with $f_0=f$ and $\partial_t|_{t=0}f_t={\rm v}$ (in the sense that $\partial_t|_{t=0}f_t(z)=v(z)$ for $z\in{\mathbb{D}}$), we have
\[\lim_{t\to0}\left\|\frac{{\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}F-{\mathbf{T}}_fF}{t} +{\mathbf{T}}_f{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm w}F\right\|_{{\mathcal{D}}(\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0)}=0,\qquad\forall\, F\in{\mathcal{D}}(\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0).\]

label: annulus_amplitude_gluing
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $g_{\mathbb{D}}:=|dz|^2$ and $g$ a metric on ${\mathbb{D}}$ extending $g_f$. We apply the gluing axiom for the free field (\cite[Theorem 4.1]{BCILT}) to ${\mathbb{A}}_f\# f({\mathbb{D}})={\mathbb{D}}$ with a magnetic insertion at $z=0$. Informally and in terms of integrals, it states that for $\widetilde{\varphi}^k\in{\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R)$ and functionals $F_1,F_2$, we have
\[\int_{\phi:{\mathbb{D}}\to{\mathbb{T}}_R}F_1(\phi|_{f({\mathbb{D}})})F_2(\phi|_{{\mathbb{A}}_f})\,{\mathrm{D}}\phi = C\int_{\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k:{\mathbb{T}}\to{\mathbb{T}}_R}\left(\int_{\phi_1:f({\mathbb{D}})\to{\mathbb{T}}_R}F_1(\phi_1)\,{\mathrm{D}}\phi_1\right)\left(\int_{\phi_2:{\mathbb{A}}_f\to{\mathbb{T}}_R}F_2(\phi_2)\,{\mathrm{D}}\phi_2\right){\mathrm{D}}\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k,\]
where the constraints on the integrals are $\phi|_{\mathbb{T}}=\widetilde{\varphi}^k$ and $\phi_1\circ f|_{\mathbb{T}}=\phi_2\circ f|_{\mathbb{T}}=\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k$, and $C=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi}$ in this case. Taking $F_1(\phi_1)=F(\phi_1\circ f|_{\mathbb{T}})$ and $F_2$ the integrand of the CILT amplitude on $({\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f)$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{annulus_amplitude_gluing}
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi} \frac{e^{-\frac{1}{4\pi} R^2k^2\int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg f^{-1}|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}}}{\sqrt{\det'\Delta_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}}}} \int_{{\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R)} {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f}(\widetilde{\varphi}^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k) \,F(\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k)\,{\mathrm{d}}\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k \\
&\quad = \frac{e^{-\frac{1}{4\pi} R^2k^2\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg\!|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}}}{\sqrt{\det'\Delta_g}}\, {\mathbb{E}}\left[F\big((P\widetilde{\varphi}^k+X_{\mathbb{D}})\circ f\big|_{{\mathbb{T}}}\big)\,e^{-\frac{{\mathrm{i}} Q}{4\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}K_{g_f}(P\widetilde{\varphi}^k+X_{\mathbb{D}})\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f}-\mu\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}M_\beta(P\widetilde{\varphi}^k+X_{\mathbb{D}},{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f})}\right],
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where the expectation is over the GFF $X_{\mathbb{D}}$, the integrals $\int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg f^{-1}|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g},\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg\!|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}$ are regularized as in \cite[Section 2.6]{BCILT} by taking the principal part, and the curvature term $\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}K_{g_f}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f}$ is regularized as in \cite[Section 5]{BCILT}.

We first compute $\int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg f^{-1}|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}-\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg\!|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}$. Since this is conformally invariant, using $g_{\mathbb{D}}$ in place of $g$, it becomes
\[\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\left(\int_{{\mathbb{D}}\setminus f^{-1}(\varepsilon{\mathbb{D}})}|d\arg\!|_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{D}}} - \int_{{\mathbb{D}}\setminus\varepsilon{\mathbb{D}}}|d\arg\!|_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}\right) = -\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\int_{f^{-1}(\varepsilon{\mathbb{D}})\setminus\varepsilon{\mathbb{D}}}\frac{{\mathrm{d}} r}{r}\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta.\]
Now $f(z)=f'(0)z+O(z^2)$ as $z\to0$, so it is not hard to see that this converges to $2\pi\log|f'(0)|$. Thus $e^{-\frac{1}{4\pi} R^2k^2\left(\int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg f^{-1}|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}-\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}^{{\mathrm{reg}}}|d\arg\!|_{g}^2\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g}\right)} = |f'(0)|^{-\frac{R^2k^2}{2}}$.

Next we claim that $\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}K_{g_f}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f}=0$ (modulo $2\pi R{\mathbb{Z}}$).                                                                                                                                         
Indeed,
\[\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}K_{g_f}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f} = \int_{{\mathbb{D}}}K_{g}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g} - \int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}K_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}},\]
where we view both ${\mathbb{D}}$ and $f({\mathbb{D}})$ as surfaces with a magnetic insertion at $0$ and tangent vector $\partial_z$. By the formula for change of conformal metric (\cite[Proposition 5.2.(4)]{BCILT}), writing $g=e^\rho\,|dz|^2$, we have
\[\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}K_{g}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g} = 2\int_{\partial{\mathbb{D}}}\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,|dz| + \int_{{\mathbb{D}}}\langle d\rho,dP\widetilde{\varphi}^k\rangle_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}\,|dz|^2.\]
We compute the first term by regularizing with respect to the separating family consisting only of the straight line segment from $0$ to $1$. Then
\[\int_{\partial{\mathbb{D}}}\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,|dz| = 2\pi c + \int_{{\mathbb{T}}}\varphi + Rk\int_0^{2\pi}\theta\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta = 2\pi(P\widetilde{\varphi})(0) + 2\pi^2Rk,\]
where we used the mean value property of harmonic functions. As for the second term, since $g_f$ is admissible, we have $\rho(z) = -2\log|z|$ near $\partial{\mathbb{D}}$, so by integration by parts,
\[\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}\langle d\rho,dP\widetilde{\varphi}^k\rangle_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}\,|dz|^2 = \int_{\partial{\mathbb{D}}} \rho\,\frac{\partial P\widetilde{\varphi}^k}{\partial\nu}\,|dz| = 0.\]
By the same token,
\[\int_{f({\mathbb{D}})}K_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}}P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}} = \int_{\mathbb{D}} K_{f^*g}(P\widetilde{\varphi}^k\circ f)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{f^*g} = 4\pi(P\widetilde{\varphi}\circ f)(0) + 2Rk\int_{-\arg f'(0)}^{2\pi-\arg f'(0)}\arg f(e^{{\mathrm{i}}\theta})\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta,\]
where we regularize on $({\mathbb{D}},f^*g)$ with respect to the separating family consisting only of the straight line segment from $0$ to $e^{-{\mathrm{i}}\arg f'(0)}$.                                                                                                                                      
Now $\arg(f(e^{-{\mathrm{i}}\arg f'(0)}z)/z)$ is well-defined and harmonic on ${\mathbb{D}}$ and its value at $0$ is $0$, so by the mean value property,
\[\int_{-\arg f'(0)}^{2\pi-\arg f'(0)}\arg f(e^{{\mathrm{i}}\theta})\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}\arg f(e^{-{\mathrm{i}}\arg f'(0)}e^{{\mathrm{i}}\theta})\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}\theta\,{\mathrm{d}}\theta=2\pi^2.\]
Thus the claim is proved.

Returning to \eqref{annulus_amplitude_gluing}, we perform the imaginary Girsanov transform (see \cite[Theorem 3.4]{BCILT}) with respect to
\[Y = -\frac{{\mathrm{i}} Q}{4\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}K_{g_f}X_{\mathbb{D}}\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f}.\]
Consider the harmonic function $h_f$ on $f({\mathbb{D}})$ defined by $h_f(f(z))=\log\frac{|zf'(z)|}{|f(z)|}$, so that $f^*g_{\mathbb{A}}=e^{2h_f\circ f}g_{\mathbb{A}}$. Note that $h_f\circ f\big|_{{\mathbb{T}}}=\log\frac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}$. Since $g_f$ is admissible, we have $g_f=e^{-2\chi_f}g_{\mathbb{A}}$ where $\chi_f\in C^\infty({\mathbb{A}}_f,{\mathbb{R}})$ is $0$ near ${\mathbb{T}}$ and equal to $h_f$ near $f({\mathbb{T}})$. We extend $\chi_f$ to ${\mathbb{D}}$ by defining it to be $h_f$ on $f({\mathbb{D}})$. Now $K_{g_f} = -2e^{2\chi_f}\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}\chi_f$, ${\mathrm{d}} v_{g_f} = e^{-2\chi_f}\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}$, so
\[{\mathbb{E}}[YX_{\mathbb{D}}] = {\mathrm{i}} Q\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}\chi_f(x)\,G(x,\cdot)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}(x) = {\mathrm{i}} Q\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}\chi_f(x)\,G(x,\cdot)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{D}}}(x) = {\mathrm{i}} Q\chi_f,\]
where $G=G_{\mathbb{D}}$ is the Green's function on ${\mathbb{D}}$ with Dirichlet boundary condition. Similarly,
\begin{align*}
{\mathbb{E}}[Y^2] &= -\frac{Q^2}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}\chi_f(x)\,G(x,y)\,\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}\chi_f(y)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}(x)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}(y) = -\frac{Q^2}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\chi_f\,\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}\chi_f\,{\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{\mathbb{A}}} \\
&= -12Q^2S_{\mathrm L}^0({\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,g_{\mathbb{A}}) - \frac{Q^2}{2\pi}\int_{f({\mathbb{T}})}\chi_f\,\frac{\partial\chi_f}{\partial\nu}\,{\mathrm{d}}\ell_{g_{\mathbb{A}}},
\end{align*}
where $\nu$ is the unit normal vector pointing towards ${\mathbb{A}}_f$. Since $\chi_f$ is harmonic in $f({\mathbb{D}})$, $\frac{\partial\chi_f}{\partial\nu}\circ f=\frac{|f|}{|f'|}{\mathbf{D}}(\chi_f\circ f|_{\mathbb{T}})$ by definition, so the last term is precisely $Q^2\left\langle{\mathbf{D}}\log\tfrac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}},\log\tfrac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\right\rangle$.

It remains to show that
\begin{equation}\label{det_formula}
\frac{\det'\Delta_g}{\det'\Delta_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}}}=e^{-\frac{1}{6}W(f,g_f)}.
\end{equation}
By \cite[Lemma 4.3]{BCILT},
\[\textstyle\det'\Delta_g = 2\pi \det'\Delta_{g|_{f({\mathbb{D}})}}\det'\Delta_{g_f}\det_{\text{Fr}}({\mathbf{D}}_{{\mathbb{D}},f({\mathbb{T}})}(2{\mathbf{D}}_0)^{-1}),\]
where the last term is a certain Fredholm determinant. The calculation at the end of the proof of \cite[Proposition 3.4]{Segal_semigroup} shows that
\[2\pi\,\frac{\det'\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}}{e^{\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{f({\mathbb{T}})}k_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}{\mathrm{d}}\ell_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}}} \det\nolimits_{\text{Fr}}({\mathbf{D}}_{{\mathbb{D}},f({\mathbb{T}})}(2{\mathbf{D}}_0)^{-1}) = e^{\frac{1}{6}\log|f'(0)|+\frac{1}{6}\left\langle{\mathbf{D}}\log\frac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}},\log\frac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\right\rangle}.\]
By the Polyakov formula (see \cite[Proposition 5.10]{Boundary_Segal} for example),
\[\det\nolimits'\Delta_{g_f} = \frac{\det'\Delta_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}}{e^{\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{f({\mathbb{T}})}k_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}{\mathrm{d}}\ell_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}}}\,e^{-2S_{\mathrm L}^0({\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,g_{\mathbb{A}})}.\]
Thus \eqref{det_formula} is proved.

label: W_additivity
title: Proof
body_md:
By the gluing axiom of CILT amplitudes (\cite[Proposition 8.13]{CILT}, \cite[Theorem 7.8]{BCILT}), it suffices to show that the functional $W$ is additive in the sense that
\begin{equation}\label{W_additivity}
W(f_1\circ f_2,g_{f_1\circ f_2}) = W(f_1,g_{f_1}) + W(f_2,g_{f_2}),
\end{equation}
where $g_{f_1\circ f_2}$ is an admissible metric on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_1\circ f_2}={\mathbb{A}}_{f_1}\# f_1({\mathbb{A}}_{f_2})$ obtained by gluing an admissible metric $g_{f_1}$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_1}$ and an admissible metric $(f_1)_*g_{f_2}$ on $f_1({\mathbb{A}}_{f_2})$. Additivity of the first term $\log|f'(0)|$ in $W$ is clear. Recall from the previous proof that
\[E(f,g_f) := \left\langle{\mathbf{D}}\log\tfrac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}},\log\tfrac{|f'|}{|f|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\right\rangle + 12S_{\mathrm L}^0({\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,g_{\mathbb{A}}) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_f}\chi_f\,\Delta_g\chi_f\,{\mathrm{d}} v_g,\]
where $g$ is any conformal metric on ${\mathbb{D}}$, and we define $h_f,\chi_f$ as in the previous proof for $f\in\{f_1,f_2,f_1\circ f_2\}$. We have
\[e^{-2\chi_{f_2}}g_{\mathbb{A}}=g_{f_2}=f_1^*g_{f_1\circ f_2}=f_1^*(e^{-2\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}}g_{\mathbb{A}})=e^{-2\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1}f_1^*g_{\mathbb{A}}=e^{-2\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1}e^{2h_{f_1}\circ f_1}g_{\mathbb{A}},\]
so
\[\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1 = h_{f_1}\circ f_1 + \chi_{f_2}\quad\text{ on }{\mathbb{A}}_{f_2}.\]
Similarly,
\[e^{2h_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1\circ f_2}g_{\mathbb{A}}=(f_1\circ f_2)^*g_{\mathbb{A}}=f_2^*(e^{2h_{f_1}\circ f_1}g_{\mathbb{A}})=e^{2h_{f_1}\circ f_1\circ f_2}e^{2h_{f_2}\circ f_2}g_{\mathbb{A}},\]
so 
\[h_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1 = h_{f_1}\circ f_1 + h_{f_2}\quad\text{ on }f_2({\mathbb{D}}).\]
Thus the identity $\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1 = h_{f_1}\circ f_1 + \chi_{f_2}$ holds on ${\mathbb{D}}$. Clearly $\chi_{f_1\circ f_2} = \chi_{f_1}$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_1}$, so
\begin{align*}
E(f_1\circ f_2,g_{f_1\circ f_2}) - E(f_1,g_{f_1}) &= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{f_1({\mathbb{A}}_{f_2})}\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\,\Delta_g\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\,{\mathrm{d}} v_g = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}(\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1)\,\Delta_g(\chi_{f_1\circ f_2}\circ f_1)\,{\mathrm{d}} v_g \\
&= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{D}}}\chi_{f_2}\,\Delta_g\chi_{f_2}\,{\mathrm{d}} v_g=E(f_2,g_{f_2}),
\end{align*}
where we used that $h_{f_1}\circ f_1$ is harmonic.

label: HilleYosida_lemma
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The quadratic form ${\mathcal{Q}}$ is strictly $m$-accretive in the sense defined in \cite[Section VIII.6]{ReedSimon}. Thus we obtain the operator ${\mathbf{H}}$ which coincides with the adjoint of the operator associated with ${\mathcal{Q}}$ as in Theorem VIII.16 (\textit{ibid.}). Using the polarization identity and the second bound in \eqref{sectorial_property}, there exists $C'>0$ such that $|{\mathcal{Q}}(u,v)|\leq C'\sqrt{{\mathcal{Q}}_0(u,u){\mathcal{Q}}_0(v,v)}$ for $u,v\in{\mathcal{D}}({\mathcal{Q}}_0)$. This shows that ${\mathbf{H}}$ is bounded as an operator ${\mathcal{D}}({\mathcal{Q}}_0)\to{\mathcal{D}}'({\mathcal{Q}}_0)$.

By the lemma following Theorem VIII.16 (\textit{ibid.}), we have that any $\lambda\in{\mathbb{C}}$ with $\operatorname{Re}\lambda<0$ is in the resolvent set of ${\mathbf{H}}$ and $\|({\mathbf{H}}-\lambda)^{-1}\|_{{\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{H}}}\leq(-\operatorname{Re}\lambda)^{-1}$. By the Hille--Yosida theorem and \cite[Theorem 2.5.2.(d)]{Pazy}, ${\mathbf{H}}$ generates an analytic contraction semigroup $t\mapsto e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}$ and we have $\|{\mathbf{H}} e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}\|_{{\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{H}}}\leq C_1/t$ ($t>0$) for some uniform $C_1>0$. In particular, ${\mathbf{H}} e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}\in{\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{H}})$. Thus for $u\in{\mathcal{H}}$, we have $\|e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u\|_{{\mathcal{D}}({\mathcal{Q}}_0)}^2={\mathcal{Q}}_0(e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u,e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u)\leq C|{\mathcal{Q}}(e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u,e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u)|=C|\langle {\mathbf{H}} e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u,e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u\rangle_{{\mathcal{H}}}|\leq C\|{\mathbf{H}} e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u\|_{\mathcal{H}}\|e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}u\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq C_2\|u\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2$ with $C_2:=C\|{\mathbf{H}} e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}\|_{{\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{H}}}\|e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}\|_{{\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{H}}}<\infty$. In other words, $e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}$ is bounded as an operator ${\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{D}}({\mathcal{Q}}_0)$. By duality (for ${\mathbf{H}}^*$), it extends to a bounded operator ${\mathcal{D}}'({\mathcal{Q}}_0)\to{\mathcal{H}}$. Thus for $t>0$, $e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}=e^{-\frac{t}{2}{\mathbf{H}}}e^{-\frac{t}{2}{\mathbf{H}}}:{\mathcal{D}}'({\mathcal{Q}}_0)\to{\mathcal{H}}\to{\mathcal{D}}({\mathcal{Q}}_0)$ is bounded.

title: Lemma
body_md: The quadratic form $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0$ is closable. We identify it with its closure and denote by ${\mathcal{D}}(\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0)$ its domain.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Clearly $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0$ is well-defined on ${\mathcal{E}}({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$. Let $(F_n)_{n=1}^\infty\subset{\mathcal{E}}({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$ be a sequence such that $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0(F_m-F_n,F_m-F_n)\to0$ as $m,n\to\infty$. Since $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0\geq\frac{\min(1,Q^2)}2\|\!\cdot\!\|_{L^2}^2$, $(F_n)_n$ is Cauchy in $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$. Suppose $\|F_n-F_0\|_{L^2}\to0$ for some $F_0\in L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$. To show that $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0$ is closable, it suffices to show that $F_0=0$ implies $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0(F_n,F_n)\to0$. Consider the Hilbert space ${\mathcal{H}}_0:=L^2({\mathbb{T}}_R\times{\mathcal{D}}_0'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{R}}))$ with the norm $\|F\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0}^2:=\int_{{\mathbb{T}}_R}{\mathbb{E}}[|F(c+\varphi)|^2]\,{\mathrm{d}} c$ (the expectation being over the mean-zero GFF $\varphi$ on ${\mathbb{T}}$) and the product Hilbert space ${\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty:=\bigoplus_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}({\mathcal{H}}_0\oplus{\mathcal{H}}_0\oplus{\mathcal{H}}_0^{{\mathbb{N}}_{\geq1}}\oplus{\mathcal{H}}_0^{{\mathbb{N}}_{\geq1}})$ with the norm
\[\|(F_k^1,F_k^2,(F_{kn}^3)_{n\geq1},(F_{kn}^4)_{n\geq1})_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty}^2:=\sum_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\left(\frac{1}{2}\|F_k^1\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0}^2+\frac{R^2k^2+Q^2}{2}\|F_k^2\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0}^2+2\sum_{n\geq1}\|F_{kn}^3\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0}^2+2\sum_{n\geq1}\|F_{kn}^4\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0}^2\right).\]
Then we have the linear map
\[\iota:F\mapsto(\partial_cF_k,F_k,({\mathbf{A}}_n F_k)_{n\geq1},(\widetilde{{\mathbf{A}}}_n F_k)_{n\geq1})_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}},\qquad F_k(c+\varphi):=F(c+\varphi+kR\arg),\]
such that $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0(F,F)=\|\iota F\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty}^2$. The condition $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0(F_m-F_n,F_m-F_n)\to0$ implies that $(\iota F_m)_m$ is Cauchy in ${\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty$, so we can assume that $\iota F_m$ converges to some $(F_k^1,F_k^2,(F_{kn}^3)_{n\geq1},(F_{kn}^4)_{n\geq1})_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\in{\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty$. In particular, ${\mathbf{A}}_n F_m\to(F_{kn}^3)_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}$ in $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))\cong\oplus_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}{\mathcal{H}}_0$. For any $G\in{\mathcal{E}}({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$, we have
\[\langle(F_{kn}^3)_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}},G\rangle=\lim_{m\to\infty}\langle {\mathbf{A}}_n F_m,G\rangle=\lim_{m\to\infty}\langle F_m,{\mathbf{A}}_{-n}G\rangle=\langle F_0,{\mathbf{A}}_{-n}G\rangle=0,\]
so $F_{kn}^3=0$ for all $k,n$. Similarly, one shows that $F_k^1=F_k^2=F_{kn}^4=0$ for all $k,n$. Thus $\iota F_m$ converges to $0$ in ${\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty$, i.e., $\widetilde{{\mathcal{Q}}}^0(F_m,F_m)=\|\iota F_m\|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0^\infty}^2\to0$.

name: \textbf{Feynman--Kac formula, free case

title: Proof
body_md:
For $k\in{\mathbb{Z}}$, let ${\mathcal{H}}_k:=L^2({\mathbb{T}}_R\times{\mathcal{D}}_0'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{R}})\times\{k\})\subset L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$, so that $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))=\bigoplus_{k\in{\mathbb{Z}}}{\mathcal{H}}_k$. Clearly all the operators above preserve each ${\mathcal{H}}_k$.

First consider the case $k=0$. To show that ${\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^0 = e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm v}^0}$ on ${\mathcal{H}}_0$, it suffices to repeat the end of the proof of \cite[Theorem 2.8]{Virasoro_structure} (more precisely, Propositions 2.11 and 2.12), \textit{mutatis mutandis}. Indeed, the calculation of $\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\big|_{t=0}F\big(P\widetilde{\varphi}\circ f_t\big|_{\mathbb{T}} + Q\log\tfrac{|f_t'|}{|f_t|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\big)$ in Proposition 2.11 (\textit{ibid.}) holds for all $Q\in{\mathbb{C}}$ if $F$ is analytic in the zero mode $c$, and the calculation of $\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\big|_{t=0}{\mathbb{E}}\big[F\big(\widetilde{\varphi} + (X_{\mathbb{D}}\circ f_t)\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\big)\big]$ in Proposition 2.12 (\textit{ibid.}) carries over verbatim since they concern the same GFF $X_{\mathbb{D}}$.

For a general $k\in{\mathbb{Z}}$, we have ${\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^0|_{{\mathcal{H}}_k} = |f_t'(0)|^{\frac{R^2k^2}{2}}\, {\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^0|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0} \circ \tau_{k,t}$, where we identify ${\mathcal{H}}_k$ and ${\mathcal{H}}_0$ via the natural isomorphism and $\tau_{k,t}$ is the translation on ${\mathcal{H}}_0$ defined by $(\tau_{k,t}F)(\widetilde{\varphi}) := F(\widetilde{\varphi} + Rkg_t|_{\mathbb{T}})$, where $g_t(z):=\arg f_t(z)-\arg z=\operatorname{Im}\log\frac{f_t(z)}{z}$. Note that $g_t$ admits a continuous branch on ${\mathbb{D}}$ and is well-defined up to a global constant in $2\pi{\mathbb{Z}}$. Thus the generator of ${\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^0|_{{\mathcal{H}}_k}$ is
\[-\frac{R^2k^2}{2}\operatorname{Re}\omega+{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm v}^0|_{{\mathcal{H}}_0} - \partial_t\big|_{t=0}\tau_{k,t}.\]
To compute the last term,
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}g_t(z) = \operatorname{Im}\frac{\partial_tf_t}{f_t}\bigg|_{t=0}(z) = \operatorname{Im} \frac{v(z)}{z} = -\operatorname{Im}\sum_{n=0}^\infty v_nz^n,\]
so
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\tau_{k,t} = Rk\left(-\operatorname{Im}\omega\,\partial_c+\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{{\mathrm{i}}}{2}(v_n\partial_n-\overline{v_n}\partial_{-n})\right).\]
The rest of the proof is a straightforward algebraic calculation.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk_tech_GMC}
    Let us explain the technical reasons why we choose this regularization instead of the usual harmonic cutoff that will be used in the paper about conformal bootstrap of CILT. In the proof of Feynman--Kac formula \cref{prop_FK_formula}, we need to find a uniform bound for the exponential moment of the regularized GMC like our \cref{lemma_gmc_delta_exp_bound} (in the real case, the potential is positive so they are free from this problem). If we use white noise decomposition as in \cref{lemma_gmc_delta_exp_bound} for the harmonic cutoff, we need to estimate the Fourier coefficient of the heat kernel accurately. Besides, the harmonic cutoff of $X\circ f_t$ can not produce a martingale, so we cannot use Jensen's inequality to finish the proof, unless we go through a detailed study of the Fourier coefficient of $\log|f_s(e^{{\mathrm{i}}\theta})-f_{s'}(e^{{\mathrm{i}}\theta'})|$. On the other hand, not every regularization is compatible with the Hilbert space $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$. Note that $V_{\rm v}^{(\delta)}$ is measurable in $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R))$, while the white noise decomposition and circle average are not. This is crucial in applying the Trotter's product formula in \cref{prop_FK_formula}.

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from \cref{T_f_differentiable} in the same way as in \cite[Section 4.3]{Segal_semigroup}, noting that taking the adjoint of CILT amplitudes requires replacing $\mu,\beta$ by $\bar{\mu},-\beta$. We give a self-contained proof here for the sake of completeness.

First we need to consider amplitudes of outer annuli. Let $\iota:z\mapsto 1/\bar{z}$ and ${\mathbb{D}}^*:=\iota({\mathbb{D}})=\hat{{\mathbb{C}}}\setminus{\mathbb{D}}^\circ$ the closed outer unit disk. Note that $\iota|_{\mathbb{T}}={\mathrm{id}}_{\mathbb{T}}$. For $f\in{\mathcal{S}}$, the map $f^\iota:=\iota\circ f\circ\iota$ is a holomorphic embedding ${\mathbb{D}}^*\to({\mathbb{D}}^*)^\circ$ with $f^\iota(\infty)=\infty$, and we associate to it the outer annulus ${\mathbb{A}}_{f^\iota}:=\iota({\mathbb{A}}_f)={\mathbb{D}}^*\setminus f^\iota(({\mathbb{D}}^*)^\circ)$ with boundary parametrizations ${\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f^\iota}:=(f^\iota|_{\mathbb{T}},{\mathrm{id}}_{{\mathbb{T}}})$. Then for an admissible metric $g_f$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_f$, we have
\[{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f^\iota},\iota_* g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f^\iota}}^{\mu,\beta} = ({\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_f,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f}^{\bar{\mu},-\beta})^*,\]
where we have made explicit the dependence on $\mu,\beta$. Indeed, by diffeomorphism invariance, we have for $\widetilde{\varphi}_1^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k\in{\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}},{\mathbb{T}}_R)$
\[{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f^\iota},\iota_* g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f^\iota}}^{\mu,\beta}(\widetilde{\varphi}_1^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k) = {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f},g_f,(f|_{\mathbb{T}},{\mathrm{id}}_{\mathbb{T}})}^{\mu,\beta}(\widetilde{\varphi}_1^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k) = {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f},g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f}^{\mu,\beta}(\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_1^k) =  \overline{{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f},g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f}^{\bar{\mu},-\beta}(\widetilde{\varphi}_2^k,\widetilde{\varphi}_1^k)}.\]
If $t\mapsto f_t\in{\mathcal{S}}$ is the flow on ${\mathbb{D}}$ generated by a Markovian holomorphic vector field ${\rm v}=-\sum_{n=0}^\infty v_nz^{n+1}\partial_z$, then $t\mapsto f_t^\iota$ is the flow on ${\mathbb{D}}^*$ generated by ${\rm v}^\iota:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\overline{v_n}z^{-n+1}\partial_z$, so that by \cref{prop_semigroup_as_amplitude},
\[\frac{e^{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{L}}}{12}W(f_t,g_{f_t})}}{\sqrt{2}\pi}{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t^\iota},\iota_* g_{f_t},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_t^\iota}}^{\mu,\beta} = ({\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^{\bar{\mu},-\beta})^* = e^{-t({\mathbf{H}}_{\rm v}^{\bar{\mu},-\beta})^*} = e^{t{\mathbf{H}}_{{\rm v}^\iota}^{\mu,\beta}},\]
where $g_{f_t}$ is any admissible metric on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}$ and we have used \eqref{L_n_adjoint}. Similarly, defining ${\mathbf{T}}_{f^\iota}^{\mu,\beta}:=({\mathbf{T}}_f^{\bar{\mu},-\beta})^*$ for $f\in{\mathcal{S}}$, we have analogously to \cref{T_f_differentiable}
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}{\mathbf{T}}_{f_t^\iota}={\mathbf{H}}_{{\rm w}^\iota}\circ{\mathbf{T}}_{f^\iota},\qquad{\rm w}=\tfrac{v(z)}{f'(z)}\partial_z,\]
where $t\mapsto f_t\in{\mathcal{S}}$ is a differentiable family with $f_0=f$ and $\partial_t|_{t=0}f_t={\rm v}$.

The proof relies on the observation that an annulus in ${\mathcal{S}}({\mathbb{A}})$ can be decomposed into an inner annulus and an outer annulus, both parametrized by ${\mathcal{S}}$. Indeed, for $f\in{\mathcal{S}}({\mathbb{A}})$, consider the closed Riemann surface $S_f:=({\mathbb{D}}^*\cup{\mathbb{A}}_f)\sqcup{\mathbb{D}}/\!\sim$ where the quotient relation is $z\in\partial{\mathbb{D}}\sim f(z)\in\partial({\mathbb{D}}^*\cup{\mathbb{A}}_f)$. This is topologically a sphere, so there exists a uniformizing biholomorphism $\Phi_f:S_f\to\hat{\mathbb{C}}$, which is unique if we require that $\Phi_f(0)=0$, $\Phi_f'(0)=a$, $\Phi_f(\infty)=\infty$, where $r<a<1$ is fixed. We apply this with $f=f_t\in{\mathcal{S}}({\mathbb{A}})$ as in the statement of the lemma and let $f_{{\rm out},t}:=\iota\circ(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}}\circ{\mathrm{id}}_{\mathbb{T}})\circ\iota$, $f_{{\rm in},t}:=\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}}\circ f_t|_{\mathbb{T}}$, which both extend to holomorphic maps on ${\mathbb{D}}$. We have $\Phi_{f_0}=\frac{a}{r}{\mathrm{id}}$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_0}$, so for $t$ small, we have ${\mathbb{T}}\subset\Phi_{f_t}({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}^\circ)$, so that $f_{{\rm out},t},f_{{\rm in},t}\in{\mathcal{S}}$. Note that $f_{{\rm out},0}=\frac{r}{a}{\mathrm{id}}$, $f_{{\rm in},0}=a\;\!{\mathrm{id}}$. Let ${\rm v}_{\rm out}:=\partial_t|_{t=0}f_{{\rm out},t}$, ${\rm v}_{\rm in}:=\partial_t|_{t=0}f_{{\rm in},t}$. Differentiating the relation $f_{{\rm out},t}^\iota\circ f_t=f_{{\rm in},t}$ on ${\mathbb{T}}$ at $t=0$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{v_in_v_out_relation}
\frac{a^2}{r^2}v_{\rm out}^\iota(rz)+\frac{a}{r}v(z)=v_{\rm in}(z),\qquad z\in{\mathbb{T}}.
\end{equation}
By conformal covariance, we may assume that
$(\Phi_{f_t})_*g_{f_t}=g_{\mathbb{A}}$ near ${\mathbb{T}}$.
Indeed, this can be achieved by a smooth conformal change
supported away from the original boundary components and vanishing
at $t=0$. Since $g_{f_0}=g_{\mathbb{A}}$ is flat, the corresponding Weyl
anomaly is $O(t^2)$, so this modification does not change the
derivative at $t=0$. Now by gluing,
\[{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_t}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi}\,{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm out},t}^\iota},\iota_*g_{f_{{\rm out},t}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_{{\rm out},t}^\iota}}\circ{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm in},t}},g_{f_{{\rm in},t}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_{{\rm in},t}}},\]
where $g_{f_{{\rm out},t}}:=\iota_*(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})_*g_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm out},t}^\iota}}$, $g_{f_{{\rm in},t}}:=(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})_*g_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm in},t}}}$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq_annulus_differential}
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\big|_{t=0}{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_t}} &= \frac{c_{\mathrm{L}}}{12}\big(\partial_t\big|_{t=0}(W(f_{{\rm out},t},g_{f_{{\rm out},t}})+W(f_{{\rm in},t},g_{f_{{\rm in},t}}))\big){\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_0},g_{\mathbb{A}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_0}}\\
&\hspace{8em}+{\mathbf{H}}_{\frac{a}{r}{\rm v}_{\rm out}^\iota}{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_0},g_{\mathbb{A}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_0}}-{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_0},g_{\mathbb{A}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_0}}{\mathbf{H}}_{\frac{1}{a}{\rm v}_{\rm in}},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where we used \cref{prop_semigroup_as_amplitude,T_f_differentiable} and the remarks above on outer annuli.

We claim that
\[{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm w}{\mathbf{T}}_{f_0}={\mathbf{T}}_{f_0}{\mathbf{H}}_{\frac{1}{r}{\rm w}(r\cdot)}\]
for any holomorphic vector field ${\rm w}=-\sum_{n\in{\mathbb{Z}}}w_nz^{n+1}\partial_z$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_0}$, so that the last two terms in \eqref{eq_annulus_differential} add up to $-{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_0},g_{\mathbb{A}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_0}}{\mathbf{H}}_{{\rm v}/r}$ by \eqref{v_in_v_out_relation}. This is equivalent to the commutation relation ${\mathbf{L}}_ne^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}=e^{-nt}e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}}{\mathbf{L}}_n$ ($n\in{\mathbb{Z}}$) with $t=-\log r$. By duality, we may assume $n\geq0$, i.e., ${\rm w}$ is holomorphic on ${\mathbb{D}}$. By linearity, it suffices to consider the case where ${\rm w}$ is Markovian. Letting $t\mapsto h_t$ be the flow generated by ${\rm w}$, we have $-{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm w}{\mathbf{T}}_{f_0}=\partial_t|_{t=0}{\mathbf{T}}_{h_t}{\mathbf{T}}_{f_0}=\partial_t|_{t=0}{\mathbf{T}}_{h_t\circ f_0}$, so it suffices to compute $\partial_t|_{t=0}(h_t\circ f_0)={\rm w}(r\cdot)$ and apply again \cref{T_f_differentiable}.

It remains to compute the factor of the first term in \eqref{eq_annulus_differential}. By definition,
\[S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm out},t}^\iota},\iota_*g_{f_{{\rm out},t}},g_{\mathbb{A}})+S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{{\rm in},t}},g_{f_{{\rm in},t}},g_{\mathbb{A}}) = S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})^*g_{\mathbb{A}}).\]
Suppose $g_{\mathbb{A}}=e^{\omega_t}g_{f_t}$, $(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})^*g_{\mathbb{A}}=e^{\omega_t+u_t}g_{f_t}$. Then
\[S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})^*g_{\mathbb{A}})-S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},g_{\mathbb{A}}) = \frac{1}{96\pi}\int_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}}\left(2\langle d\omega_t,du_t\rangle_{g_{f_t}}+|du_t|_{g_{f_t}}^2+2K_{g_{f_t}}u_t\right){\mathrm{d}} v_{g_{f_t}}.\]
Since $\omega_0=u_0=0$, $K_{g_{f_0}}=K_{g_{\mathbb{A}}}=0$, we obtain $\partial_t\big|_{t=0}S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},(\Phi_{f_t}|_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_t}})^*g_{\mathbb{A}})=\partial_t\big|_{t=0}S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_t},g_{f_t},g_{\mathbb{A}})$.
By \eqref{v_in_v_out_relation} again,
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\big(\log|f_{{\rm out},t}'(0)|+\log|f_{{\rm in},t}'(0)|\big) = \operatorname{Re}\Big(\frac{a}{r}v_{\rm out}'(0)+\frac{1}{a}v_{\rm in}'(0)\Big) = -\frac{\operatorname{Re} v_0}{r}.\]
Finally, we have $\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\big\langle{\mathbf{D}}\log\frac{|f_{{\rm out},t}'|}{|f_{{\rm out},t}|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}},\log\frac{|f_{{\rm out},t}'|}{|f_{{\rm out},t}|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}\big\rangle=0$ since ${\mathbf{D}}\log\frac{|f_{{\rm out},0}'|}{|f_{{\rm out},0}|}\big|_{\mathbb{T}}=0$, and similarly for $f_{{\rm in},t}$.

name: \textbf{Ward identity

title: Proof
body_md:
See \cite[Corollary 4.8]{block} for the counterpart in real Liouville CFT; both the statement and the proof are parallel.
Consider the closed Riemann surface $\hat{\Sigma}$ obtained by gluing a disk ${\mathbb{D}}$ or ${\mathbb{D}}^*$ along each boundary circle $\zeta_j({\mathbb{T}})\subset\partial\Sigma$ via $\zeta_j$. We extend ${\rm w}$ to a neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $\hat{\Sigma}$. For $t$ small, the flow $t\mapsto f_t$ of ${\rm w}$ exists near $\Sigma$, and $(f_t)_*g$ is well-defined. By diffeomorphism invariance, ${\mathcal{A}}_{f_t(\Sigma),(f_t)_*g,(f_t)_*{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},f_t\circ{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}={\mathcal{A}}_{\Sigma,g,{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}$ is constant in $t$. We shall compute the derivative $\partial_t\big|_{t=0}{\mathcal{A}}_{f_t(\Sigma),(f_t)_*g,(f_t)_*{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},f_t\circ{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}=0$ in another way. For notational simplicity, suppose ${\mathfrak{b}}^+=0$, i.e., all boundaries are incoming. The general case follows from the analog of \cref{annulus_differential} for outer annuli, obtained by taking suitable adjoints.

Now each $\zeta_j$ extends to a holomorphic embedding ${\mathbb{D}}\to\hat{\Sigma}$. Take $r<1$ such that each $\zeta_j$ extends to a holomorphic embedding $r^{-1}{\mathbb{D}}\to\hat{\Sigma}$. Let ${\boldsymbol{\xi}}=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_{\mathfrak{b}})$ where $\xi_j=\zeta_j(r^{-1}\cdot)$ for each $j$. Let $\Sigma_0:=\Sigma\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^{\mathfrak{b}}\xi_j({\mathbb{D}}^\circ)$ with boundary parametrizations ${\boldsymbol{\xi}}|_{{\mathbb{T}}}$. By admissibility and shrinking $r$ if necessary, we may assume that $\xi_j^*g=g_{\mathbb{A}}$ on $\{r-\varepsilon<|z|<1+\varepsilon\}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, so that in particular $g|_{\Sigma_0}$ is admissible. For each $j$, let $f_{j,t}:=\xi_j^{-1}\circ f_t\circ\zeta_j\in{\mathcal{S}}({\mathbb{A}})$ and $g_{f_{j,t}}$ an admissible metric on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}$ depending in a $C^1$ fashion on $t$ with $g_{f_{j,0}}=g_{\mathbb{A}}=|dz|^2/|z|^2$. We have $f_{j,0}:z\mapsto rz$ and $\partial_t|_{t=0}f_{j,t}=r{\rm w}_j$. Let $g_t$ be the metric on $f_t(\Sigma)$ such that $g_t|_{\Sigma_0}=g|_{\Sigma_0}$ and $\xi_j^*g_t=g_{f_{j,t}}$ for each $j$. By gluing,
\[{\mathcal{A}}_{f_t(\Sigma),g_t,(f_t)_*{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},f_t\circ{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}} = C{\mathcal{A}}_{\Sigma_0,g|_{\Sigma_0},(f_t)_*{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},{\boldsymbol{\xi}}|_{\mathbb{T}}} \circ \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\mathfrak{b}} {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}},g_{f_{j,t}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_{f_{j,t}}},\]
where $C$ is a constant depending only on ${\mathfrak{b}}$. Thus
\begin{align*}
0 &= \partial_t\big|_{t=0}{\mathcal{A}}_{f_t(\Sigma),(f_t)_*g,(f_t)_*{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},f_t\circ{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}\\
&= \left(c_{\mathrm{L}}\partial_t\big|_{t=0}S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(f_t(\Sigma),g_t,(f_t)_*g)+\sum_{j=1}^{\mathfrak{s}}\big(-\Delta_{\alpha_j,m_j}\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\rho_t(z_j)+W_{\mathbf{v}}^{(j)}\big)\right) {\mathcal{A}}_{\Sigma,g,{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}\\
&\phantom{={}}+\sum_{j=1}^{\mathfrak{b}}\left(-c_{\mathrm{L}}\left(-\frac{\operatorname{Re} w_{j0}}{12}+\partial_t\big|_{t=0}S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}},g_{f_{j,t}}, g_{\mathbb{A}})\right){\mathcal{A}}_{\Sigma,g,{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}} - {\mathcal{A}}_{\Sigma,g,{\mathbf{v}},{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},{\mathbf{m}},{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}}\circ{\mathbf{H}}_{{\rm w}_j}^{(j)}\right),
\end{align*}
where $(f_t)_*g=e^{\rho_t}g_t$ and we used the Weyl anomaly formula (\cite[Proposition 8.12]{CILT}, \cite[Theorem 7.6]{BCILT}) and \cref{annulus_differential}. Note that $t\mapsto f_t$ is also the flow generated by the real vector field $W=2\operatorname{Re}(w(z)\partial_z)$. Since $g_t=g_0$ on $\Sigma_0$, we have $\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\rho_t=-\operatorname{div}_gW$ on $\Sigma_0$. It remains to collect the $S_{\mathrm{L}}^0$ terms, which give $c_{\mathrm{L}}$ times
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}\left(S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(f_t(\Sigma),g_t,(f_t)_*g)-\sum_{j=1}^{\mathfrak{b}} S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}},g_{f_{j,t}}, g_{\mathbb{A}})\right).\]
For each $j$,
\[S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(\xi_j({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}),g_t,(f_t)_*g)-S_{\mathrm{L}}^0({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}},g_{f_{j,t}}, g_{\mathbb{A}}) = S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(\xi_j({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}),g_t,(f_t)_*g)-S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(\xi_j({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}),g_t,g) = S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(\xi_j({\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}),g,(f_t)_*g),\]
where we used $\xi_j^*g=g_{\mathbb{A}}$ on ${\mathbb{A}}_{f_{j,t}}$ for $t$ small. Since $g_t=g$ on $\Sigma_0$, the above is equal to
\[\partial_t\big|_{t=0}S_{\mathrm{L}}^0(f_t(\Sigma),g,(f_t)_*g)=-\frac{1}{96\pi}\int_\Sigma 2K_g\operatorname{div}_gW\,{\mathrm{d}} v_g.\qedhere\]

\mbox{}\label{thm_BCILT_semigroup}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\emph{(\arabic*)}]
\item Let $f\in{\mathcal{S}}^+$ and $g_f$ a Neumann extendible admissible metric on ${\mathbb{A}}_f^+$ (i.e., it is the restriction to ${\mathbb{A}}_f^+$ of an even admissible metric on ${\mathbb{A}}_f$). Viewing the BCILT amplitude ${\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_f^+,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f^+}$ of $({\mathbb{A}}_f^+,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f^+)$ as an operator $L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}}^+,{\mathbb{T}}_R))\to L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}}^+,{\mathbb{T}}_R))$, we have
\[{\mathbf{T}}_f^+=\frac{e^{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{L}}}{12}W^+(f,g_f)}}{(2\pi)^{3/4}}{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{A}}_f^+,g_f,{\boldsymbol{\zeta}}_f^+},\]
where $W^+(f,g_f):=\frac{1}{2}W(f,g_f)$ with $W$ as in \cref{prop_semigroup_as_amplitude}.
\item The map $f\in{\mathcal{S}}^+\mapsto {\mathbf{T}}_f^+\in{\mathcal{L}}(L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}}^+,{\mathbb{T}}_R)))$ is a semigroup homomorphism, i.e., ${\mathbf{T}}_{f_1}^+\circ{\mathbf{T}}_{f_2}^+={\mathbf{T}}_{f_1\circ f_2}^+$ for $f_1,f_2\in{\mathcal{S}}^+$.
\item Let ${\rm v}= -\sum_{n=0}^\infty v_n z^{n+1} \partial_z$ be a symmetric Markovian holomorphic vector field on ${\mathbb{D}}$ such that \eqref{omega_condition} holds for some $K>0$ large enough. Let $t\mapsto f_t$ be the flow generated by ${\rm v}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
For $t>0$, we have $e^{-t{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm v}^+}={\mathbf{T}}_{f_t}^+$.
\item The map $f\in{\mathcal{S}}^+\mapsto {\mathbf{T}}_f^+\in{\mathcal{L}}(L^2({\mathcal{D}}'({\mathbb{T}}^+,{\mathbb{T}}_R)))$ is continuous and differentiable with differential
\[D_{\rm v}{\mathbf{T}}_f^+ = -{\mathbf{T}}_f^+\circ{\mathbf{H}}_{\rm w}^+,\qquad {\rm w} = \tfrac{v(z)}{f'(z)}\,\partial_z.\]
\end{enumerate}
